chapters.title: The Model Is Not the Behavior
Reason About Tokens, Attention, and Generation

figures.alt: A model core sits inside context, software, evaluation, user, and authority shells.
figures.evidenceRole: Visualizes the observation-versus-system claim, not a causal architecture measurement.

figures.alt: Separate specialists own distinct stations around one LLM system and an authority gate.
figures.evidenceRole: Makes the authority boundary inspectable without claiming an organizational standard.

figures.alt: Mosaic Desk proposes a next step, while a human decision gate controls the consequence.
figures.evidenceRole: Grounds the consequence and authority boundary in the task contract.

figures.alt: Six shape-distinguished behavior states surround the language-task contract.
figures.evidenceRole: Turns intended behavior into caseable states; it is not measured performance.

figures.alt: Text passes through tokenization and contextual computation to next-token probabilities.
figures.evidenceRole: Depicts the bounded generation chain without treating attention as a complete explanation.

figures.alt: Three decoding routes cross the same probability landscape.
figures.evidenceRole: Supports configuration sensitivity without promising deterministic equivalence.

limitations: Mosaic Desk is fictional and synthetic; this batch reports no production outcome.
Figure records are semantic anchors only; no image asset exists until root runs ImageGen.
Numeric release thresholds remain calibration decisions based on representative evidence.
Managed and open-weight paths share behavior evidence requirements but expose different operational responsibilities.
Maintained documentation and any selected runtime configuration must be rechecked at publication.
